title: Robot Brains, Explained: How Vision-Language-Action Models Teach Machines to Work
deck_short: The model that lets a robot see, understand words, and move — and why it still drops things.

hero.alt: A humanoid robot on a car factory line, reaching into a bin of metal brackets and placing one into a tray in the right order
hero.caption: A vision-language-action model turns a camera image and a spoken instruction into the robot’s next move — that is the whole job.
hero.index_alt: A humanoid robot on a car factory line, reaching into a bin of metal brackets
hero.index_caption: Today’s lesson: robot brains — the model that lets a machine see, understand words, and move.

title: AI Agents, Explained: What They Are, How They Work, and Why Siri Wants to Be One
deck_short: A chatbot answers you. An agent does the job. The difference, the loop behind it, and the honest state of things.

hero.alt: A small robot assistant thinking at a desk, choosing between tools — a browser, code, a calendar, a database and a search — while it works toward a goal
hero.caption: An agent is given a goal and picks its own tools to reach it. The model decides the next step — that is the whole difference.
hero.index_alt: A small robot assistant thinking at a desk, choosing between tools — a browser, code, a calendar, a database and a search
hero.index_caption: Today’s lesson: AI agents — what they are, how they work, and why Siri wants to be one.
